title: I-5 and Highway 99 in California: The Old Road
meta: How I-5 and old Highway 99 relate in California, from the Newhall Pass truck lanes to Old Highway 99 near Weed, with stops along the way.
intro: Before I-5, US 99 was the main West Coast highway, created in 1926 and running from the Mexican border to the Canadian border. This guide follows the places along I-5 where Highway 99 still shows up, from the truck lanes at exit 162 to Old Highway 99 near exit 755. I-5 Buddy tells these stories out loud as you drive.

faq.a: US 99 was created in 1926 and ran from the Mexican border to the Canadian border, and it was the main West Coast highway before I-5. It was called the Main Street of California.

faq.q: Where do I-5 and Highway 99 meet?
faq.a: They meet at the Wheeler Ridge interchange, at exit 221. Local groups pushed for a west side freeway as early as 1945, and when the Interstate system was created in 1956, it won out over turning Highway 99 into the Interstate.

faq.q: Where can I still see part of the old US 99 along I-5?
faq.a: At exit 162, the separate truck lanes that loop around the main lanes at the Newhall Pass Interchange are the original four-lane freeway, built as US 99. Near exit 755, a two-lane county road called Old Highway 99 runs between Weed and Yreka in the same form it had when it was US 99.

faq.q: What happened to old Highway 99 near Shasta Lake?
faq.a: Before the lake, old Highway 99 ran through Mountain Gate and then plunged into the valley that Shasta Lake now fills. The landmark at exit 688 is called The drowned highway.

faq.q: Who got stopped for speeding on Highway 99 near I-5?
faq.a: On September 30, 1955, a Highway Patrol officer pulled over the actor James Dean on Highway 99 near exit 225 and wrote him a speeding ticket. He was driving north, on his way to a sports car race in Salinas.
